summary.en: Reuse typed containers and methods with bounds, wildcards and an understanding of erasure.
summary.bn: টাইপের সীমা আর অজানা টাইপের নিয়ম বুঝে জেনেরিক ক্লাস ও মেথড ব্যবহার করো।

notes: All programs use Java 17 APIs and language rules.

sections.title: Separate declared type from object identity
Accept producers and consumers without unsafe casts
Use Java 17 without relying on reified type arguments
Use types to connect inputs and results

examples.title: Store a typed value
examples.explanationHtml: The box accepts text. Its get result supports String.length without a cast.

examples.title: Add values through a Number bound
examples.explanationHtml: The bound provides doubleValue, so the same method handles integer and decimal lists.

examples.title: Copy from a producer into a consumer
examples.explanationHtml: The source yields integers and the Number list can safely consume them.

examples.title: Observe erased class identity
examples.explanationHtml: Different source type arguments still share the same runtime class.

practice.title: Swap a generic pair
practice.statementHtml: Read two integers in -1000..1000. Store them in Pair<Integer> and print them in reverse order separated by one space. No prompt.
hints: Let the pair hold two values of the same parameter type.

practice.title: Transfer into a wider list
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..20) then n integers (-100..100). Write a generic transfer method using extends and super. Copy into List<Number> and print its bracketed list form. No prompt.
hints: Use one T to connect source elements to the target.

practice.title: Repair an invariant assignment
practice.statementHtml: A method expects List<Number> but only reads doubleValue(). How can it accept List<Integer>?
practice.answerHtml: Change the parameter to List<? extends Number>. Every element is readable as Number, but the method must not add arbitrary numeric values. This widening view avoids an unsafe cast.

practice.title: Explain an erased overload clash
practice.statementHtml: Why cannot show(List<String>) and show(List<Integer>) be the only distinguishing overloads?
practice.answerHtml: Both erase to show(List). Use distinct method names such as showNames and showMarks, or one generic operation if their behaviour is the same.

quiz.prompt: What String operation is available after reading Box<String>?
quiz.explanation: get returns String statically; CSE has three UTF-16 code units.

quiz.prompt: What values reach the Number destination through the wildcard copy?
quiz.explanation: The upper bound permits reads and the lower bound permits Integer additions.

quiz.prompt: Do two Box type arguments create two runtime classes?
quiz.explanation: Erasure gives both objects the same runtime Box class.

quiz.prompt: Why is List<Integer> not a List<Number>?
options: The latter would allow adding a Double
quiz.explanation: Invariance prevents writes that would violate the original list type.

quiz.prompt: Which argument replaces T when primitive int values are needed?
quiz.explanation: Type arguments require reference types; boxing can bridge int and Integer.

quiz.prompt: What can a List<? extends Number> safely produce?
options: Only Object methods on a primitive
quiz.explanation: An unknown subtype can always be viewed as Number.

quiz.prompt: What can be added to List<? super Integer>?
quiz.explanation: Every allowed target element type can accept Integer.

quiz.prompt: Why cannot a method allocate new T()?
options: Erasure does not provide a concrete constructor
quiz.explanation: A type parameter is not a concrete class name at runtime.

quiz.prompt: Which declaration introduces a method type parameter?
quiz.explanation: The angle-bracket declaration precedes the return type.

quiz.prompt: Why do overloads on List<String> and List<Integer> clash?
options: Their erased parameter types are equal
String and Integer have equal hash codes
quiz.explanation: Erasure removes the distinguishing element arguments from the method signature.

quiz.prompt: Can List<?> safely accept an arbitrary new Object?
quiz.explanation: The unknown actual argument may be String or Integer, so arbitrary Object additions are unsafe.

quiz.prompt: What can be read from List<? super Integer> without a cast?
quiz.explanation: The actual list could be List<Object> containing unrelated values.

keyPoints.bn: টাইপ প্যারামিটার দিয়ে সম্পর্কিত ডেটার টাইপ এক রাখা যায়।

keyPoints.en: Use wrapper types as generic arguments.
keyPoints.bn: জেনেরিক টাইপ আর্গুমেন্টে প্রিমিটিভের বদলে র‍্যাপার টাইপ দাও।
List<Integer>-কে সরাসরি List<Number> হিসেবে ধরতে পারবে না।

keyPoints.en: Read with extends and write with super when the contract fits.
keyPoints.bn: ডেটা পড়ার জন্য extends আর যোগ করার জন্য super কাজে লাগে।

keyPoints.en: Erasure limits runtime tests of type arguments.
keyPoints.bn: কম্পাইলের পরে টাইপ আর্গুমেন্ট মুছে যাওয়াকে erasure বলে, তাই রানটাইমে সব আর্গুমেন্ট যাচাই করা যায় না।

examQuestions.question: Explain producer extends and consumer super for an integer copy method.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The source may contain an Integer subtype and yields Integer values. The destination must accept Integer values and may use Number or Object as its element type. An extends source and super destination express those roles.

examQuestions.question: Why does Box<String>.get() need no visible cast?
examQuestions.answerHtml: The compiler checks the String argument and inserts needed casts after erasure. The caller sees a String-returning contract.

examQuestions.question: Compare List<?> and List<Object> when adding a String.
examQuestions.answerHtml: List<Object> accepts a String. List<?> may be an Integer list, so that addition is rejected. The wildcard is an unknown type, not a promise to accept every Object.
